l.i: esse: non es scriptus in numero Electorum?

main_text.l: Nemo, qui audit promissionem, indè
causam habet dubitandi de veritate; ni-
si in seipso. Neque enim Deum accusa-
re potest, non-dantem facultatem am-
plectendi non-promissam: Et, qui non
amplectitur, cum voluptate, vel saltem
studio, non amplectitur. Saul enim, ut fa-
tetur, volens effudit Spiritum Sanctum: vo-
lens moventi Spiritui Sancto repugnavit;
quod minimè debebat. Indè ergo, ut
à posteriore, colligimus, eum electum
non fuisse. Sic ipse vult Melanchthon,
dicens: Ergo, ut in justificatione diximus, ali-
quam esse in accipiente causam: non dignitatem;
(An dignitatem non spectat, qui
causam electionis moventem quærit in
homine? ut quærit, qui prævisam fidem,
vel infidelitatem, causam fingit) sed quia
Sanctus simul est efficax: (at non in omni-
bus; sed tantùm electis) ut Paulus inquit:

The transcription is partly reconstructed from a low-resolution scan: the sentence "Nemo, qui audit promissionem..." and surrounding lines are uncertain; words such as "promissionem", "non-dantem", "non-promissam" and "volens" in the middle paragraph may be misread and should be checked against the original. Marked passages are not guaranteed exact. The paragraph structure of the running text is approximate, and the note-like lines beginning with a small mark ("»") at the left margin of the column (lines "studio, non amplectitur" through "sed tantùm electis") are a printed run of text in the column with marginal quotation marks, not separate notes.
